1	"""Inventory constants (STRUCTURE §3): enums (UPPER_SNAKE values stored as strings) and the
2	permission keys, registered into the core RBAC catalog at import (D-009).
3	
4	Started as a SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line
5	cap, the finance precedent); it sits well under that for PLAN 5.1.
6	
7	Item codes are USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant (the ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, item_code)`` on
8	inv_items) — mirroring how chart-of-accounts codes work (Account.code is required on create, not
9	auto-numbered). So item/warehouse/bin MASTERS carry no gapless document number (codes, not
10	numbers). Stock MOVES (PLAN 5.2) DO register documents and claim a gapless number — the
11	``inventory.stock_move`` sequence below — because a move is a posted document in the D-012 sense.
12	"""
13	
14	from enum import StrEnum
15	
16	from app.core.rbac import register_permissions
17	
18	# Quantity scale (D-015): QuantityType stores scale-6 micro-units. Stock moves and quants use the
19	# same scale; the on-hand>=0 CHECK and the quant sums are exact on both engines.
20	
21	
22	class ItemType(StrEnum):
23	    """What an item IS, which decides whether it carries stock (D-020).
24	
25	    - STOCKED: a physical good tracked in inventory — the only type that participates in stock
26	      moves, costing and lot/serial tracking.
27	    - NON_STOCKED: a purchasable/sellable good NOT held in inventory (e.g. drop-ship, expensed
28	      supplies) — no on-hand quantity, no costing layer.
29	    - SERVICE: a non-physical line item (labour, fees) — never stocked, never tracked.
30	
31	    The service rejects tracking/costing participation for NON_STOCKED/SERVICE so the invariant
32	    "only STOCKED items have stock" holds from the masters up (validated again when moves land)."""
33	
34	    STOCKED = "STOCKED"
35	    NON_STOCKED = "NON_STOCKED"
36	    SERVICE = "SERVICE"
37	
38	
39	class CostingMethod(StrEnum):
40	    """How a stocked item is valued (D-020). Defaulted onto the item FROM its category at create
41	    but STORED on the item, because D-020 changes it only while no stock exists and the item is
42	    the costing unit. The moving-average valuation table and FIFO cost layers arrive in PLAN 5.3;
43	    5.1 only records the method so receipts know which engine to use."""
44	
45	    MOVING_AVERAGE = "MOVING_AVERAGE"
46	    FIFO = "FIFO"
47	
48	
49	class TrackingMode(StrEnum):
50	    """Whether a stocked item's units are individually identified (parity: batch/serial mgmt).
51	
52	    - NONE: fungible — quantity only (the default).
53	    - LOT: grouped by lot/batch code; one lot row per received batch (inv_lots), created at
54	      receipt (5.2+).
55	    - SERIAL: each unit uniquely identified; one inv_serials row per unit, created at receipt.
56	
57	    Tracking is PER ITEM and only meaningful for STOCKED items — the service forbids a non-NONE
58	    mode on NON_STOCKED/SERVICE items."""
59	
60	    NONE = "NONE"
61	    LOT = "LOT"
62	    SERIAL = "SERIAL"
63	
64	
65	class LotStatus(StrEnum):
66	    """Lifecycle of a lot/batch instance (parity: batch management). For 5.1 the table merely
67	    EXISTS — lots are created during receipts (5.2+); AVAILABLE is the default a receipt sets,
68	    the others are reached by later quality/expiry flows. No dead CRUD now (masters-only)."""
69	
70	    AVAILABLE = "AVAILABLE"
71	    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
72	    CONSUMED = "CONSUMED"
73	
74	
75	class SerialStatus(StrEnum):
76	    """Lifecycle of a serial-number instance (parity: serial management). Like LotStatus, the
77	    table exists for 5.1 and is populated at receipt (5.2+): IN_STOCK on receipt, ISSUED when
78	    the unit leaves, BLOCKED by quality holds."""
79	
80	    IN_STOCK = "IN_STOCK"
81	    ISSUED = "ISSUED"
82	    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
83	
84	
85	class MoveType(StrEnum):
86	    """The kind of stock movement (PLAN 5.2). The move's QUANTITY is always positive; the TYPE
87	    decides which of from_bin/to_bin participate (the direction), so a single signed-quantity
88	    column is never needed (the journal one-side-CHECK philosophy applied to stock):
89	
90	    - RECEIPT: stock enters a bin from outside inventory (purchase receipt, opening balance,
91	      positive count adjustment). to_bin REQUIRED, from_bin must be NULL.
92	    - ISSUE: stock leaves a bin to outside inventory (goods issue, scrap, negative count).
93	      from_bin REQUIRED, to_bin must be NULL.
94	    - TRANSFER: stock moves between two bins, conserving total on-hand. BOTH bins REQUIRED and
95	      they must differ.
96	    - ADJUSTMENT: a one-sided correction not tied to a business document. EXACTLY ONE of
97	      from_bin (a decrease) / to_bin (an increase) is set — the side carries the signed intent
98	      while quantity stays positive (a decrease is from_bin-only, an increase is to_bin-only)."""
99	
100	    RECEIPT = "RECEIPT"
101	    ISSUE = "ISSUE"
102	    TRANSFER = "TRANSFER"
103	    ADJUSTMENT = "ADJUSTMENT"
104	
105	
106	class MoveStatus(StrEnum):
107	    """Lifecycle of a stock move (PLAN 5.2). Unlike journal entries (DRAFT→POSTED), a stock move
108	    is created already POSTED and is IMMUTABLE: the move ledger IS the single source of truth for
109	    quantity, so a move never has a draft phase and is never edited or deleted — corrections are
110	    REVERSING moves (an opposite move linked via docflow, the append-only ledger philosophy of
111	    D-017 applied to stock). The column exists for symmetry with the rest of the platform and to
112	    leave room for a future draft/scheduled-move lifecycle, but every move 5.2 creates is POSTED."""
113	
114	    POSTED = "POSTED"
115	
116	
117	# Required bin sides per move type (PLAN 5.2): (from_bin_required, to_bin_required). ADJUSTMENT is
118	# the special case — exactly one side, validated separately (the service checks the XOR). Used by
119	# the create-move validator so the rule lives in ONE place, greppable and testable.
120	MOVE_BIN_SIDES: dict[MoveType, tuple[bool, bool]] = {
121	    MoveType.RECEIPT: (False, True),
122	    MoveType.ISSUE: (True, False),
123	    MoveType.TRANSFER: (True, True),
124	    # ADJUSTMENT: not in the strict table — the service enforces "exactly one side set".
125	}
126	
127	
128	# Stock-move document type + number sequence (D-012): a move registers in core_documents and
129	# claims its gapless number AT CREATION (a move is permanent at creation — POSTED immediately —
130	# so it is numbered immediately, the orders/receipts claim-timing branch, not the draft branch).
131	# The sequence year-resets (STK-2026-00001).
132	STOCK_MOVE_DOC_TYPE = "inventory.stock_move"
133	STOCK_MOVE_SEQUENCE_NAME = "inventory.stock_move"
134	STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PREFIX = "STK"
135	STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PADDING = 5
136	
137	# docflow link type joining a reversing move to the move it reverses (D-012 vocabulary): a
138	# correction is a NEW move, never an edit, so the ledger stays append-only.
139	STOCK_MOVE_REVERSES_LINK = "reverses"
140	
141	
142	# --- Costing (PLAN 5.3, D-020/D-037) ------------------------------------------
143	# The domain-event key inventory publishes when a move changes valuation (D-011). finance/handlers
144	# subscribes and posts the COGS/inventory journal in the SAME transaction (D-020). One key carrying
145	# the move_type; the handler branches on it for the per-move-type postings.
146	STOCK_VALUED_EVENT_KEY = "inventory.stock.valued"
147	
148	# docflow link type joining a stock move's document to the journal entry the costing event posts
149	# (D-012 vocabulary): the move "posts" the valuation journal, mirroring finance's own 'posts' edge.
150	STOCK_MOVE_POSTS_LINK = "posts"
151	
152	
153	# --- Physical & cycle counts (PLAN 5.4, D-038) --------------------------------
154	class CountType(StrEnum):
155	    """What a stock count covers (parity: physical inventory vs cycle counting).
156	
157	    - PHYSICAL: a whole-warehouse snapshot — every quant in the warehouse becomes a count line.
158	    - CYCLE: a chosen subset — the caller picks the items and/or bins to count (the recurring
159	      ABC-style spot count), so only quants matching that scope become lines.
160	
161	    The type only changes which quants are enumerated into lines at populate time; the post path
162	    is identical (variance → ADJUSTMENT move) for both."""
163	
164	    PHYSICAL = "PHYSICAL"
165	    CYCLE = "CYCLE"
166	
167	
168	class CountStatus(StrEnum):
169	    """Lifecycle of a stock count (PLAN 5.4):
170	
171	    - DRAFT: created, scope chosen, lines snapshotted (system_qty captured, counted_qty NULL).
172	    - COUNTING: at least one counted quantity recorded — the warehouse team is entering counts.
173	    - POSTED: variances posted as ADJUSTMENT moves; TERMINAL — a posted count is never re-posted
174	      or cancelled (corrections are NEW counts/adjustments, the append-only ledger philosophy).
175	    - CANCELLED: abandoned before posting (only from DRAFT/COUNTING)."""
176	
177	    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
178	    COUNTING = "COUNTING"
179	    POSTED = "POSTED"
180	    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
181	
182	
183	# Count document type + number sequence (D-012): a count registers in core_documents and claims its
184	# gapless CNT number AT CREATION (a count is a real document the moment it exists — its number is
185	# the stable handle the warehouse team references while counting, so it is claimed at creation, the
186	# orders/receipts branch, not the draft-numbered-at-post branch). Year-resets (CNT-2026-00001).
187	STOCK_COUNT_DOC_TYPE = "inventory.stock_count"
188	STOCK_COUNT_SEQUENCE_NAME = "inventory.count"
189	STOCK_COUNT_NUMBER_PREFIX = "CNT"
190	STOCK_COUNT_NUMBER_PADDING = 5
191	
192	# docflow link type joining a count's document to each ADJUSTMENT move it generates at post (D-012
193	# vocabulary): the count "counts" the move into existence — the variance-posting edge the DocFlow
194	# viewer renders from the count to its adjustment moves.
195	STOCK_COUNT_ADJUSTMENT_LINK = "counts"
196	
197	# Background-job threshold (PERFORMANCE §3): a count whose post would generate more than this many
198	# variance (non-zero) lines runs as an 'inventory.count_post' job (202 {job_id}); at or below it the
199	# post runs inline (201) — mirroring the depreciation-run (100) / bank-import (1000) precedent. Each
200	# variance is a real ADJUSTMENT document, so the post is O(N) moves; above this count the request is
201	# backgrounded so it cannot hit a proxy timeout.
202	COUNT_POST_SYNC_MAX_VARIANCES = 200
203	
204	# The background-job type for a large count post (code-defined registry key, like the permission
205	# catalog — a job type exists because a handler for it ships in the codebase).
206	COUNT_POST_JOB = "inventory.count_post"
207	
208	# The currency the COGS/inventory valuation journal posts in when the tenant has not configured a
209	# functional currency (the v1 single-currency default, mirroring the journal tests' USD/2-dp). When
210	# a functional currency IS configured the handler uses it; either way costs quantize to its decimals
211	# (D-015). Stored layer/valuation costs keep full scale-6 precision — only the posted COGS rounds.
212	DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY = "USD"
213	
214	
215	# --- Permissions (D-009): one key per guarded endpoint action -----------------
216	INVENTORY_ITEM_READ = "inventory.item.read"
217	INVENTORY_ITEM_MANAGE = "inventory.item.manage"
218	INVENTORY_CATEGORY_READ = "inventory.category.read"
219	INVENTORY_CATEGORY_MANAGE = "inventory.category.manage"
220	INVENTORY_UOM_READ = "inventory.uom.read"
221	INVENTORY_UOM_MANAGE = "inventory.uom.manage"
222	# Warehouses + bins (PLAN 5.2): reference data — read vs create/edit.
223	INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_READ = "inventory.warehouse.read"
224	INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_MANAGE = "inventory.warehouse.manage"
225	INVENTORY_BIN_READ = "inventory.bin.read"
226	INVENTORY_BIN_MANAGE = "inventory.bin.manage"
227	# Stock moves (PLAN 5.2): read the move ledger + on-hand vs create a move (which is POSTED and
228	# changes on-hand, so it is its own action — the journal.post precedent).
229	INVENTORY_MOVE_READ = "inventory.move.read"
230	INVENTORY_MOVE_CREATE = "inventory.move.create"
231	# Stock valuation visibility (PLAN 5.3): reading the moving-average/FIFO valuation + cost layers is
232	# its own read action (a finance-adjacent concern — value, not just quantity), distinct from the
233	# move-ledger read so the value views can be granted to costing/controlling roles independently.
234	INVENTORY_VALUATION_READ = "inventory.valuation.read"
235	# Physical/cycle counts (PLAN 5.4): read counts/variances vs create+edit a count (scope, snapshot,
236	# record counted qty) vs POST it (the privileged action — posting variances changes on-hand AND
237	# posts GL journals via the 5.3 path, so it is its own key, the journal.post / depreciation.run
238	# precedent).
239	INVENTORY_COUNT_READ = "inventory.count.read"
240	INVENTORY_COUNT_MANAGE = "inventory.count.manage"
241	INVENTORY_COUNT_POST = "inventory.count.post"
242	
243	register_permissions(
244	    INVENTORY_ITEM_READ,
245	    INVENTORY_ITEM_MANAGE,
246	    INVENTORY_CATEGORY_READ,
247	    INVENTORY_CATEGORY_MANAGE,
248	    INVENTORY_UOM_READ,
249	    INVENTORY_UOM_MANAGE,
250	    INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_READ,
251	    INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_MANAGE,
252	    INVENTORY_BIN_READ,
253	    INVENTORY_BIN_MANAGE,
254	    INVENTORY_MOVE_READ,
255	    INVENTORY_MOVE_CREATE,
256	    INVENTORY_VALUATION_READ,
257	    INVENTORY_COUNT_READ,
258	    INVENTORY_COUNT_MANAGE,
259	    INVENTORY_COUNT_POST,
260	    descriptions={
261	        INVENTORY_ITEM_READ: "Read items and their UoM conversions",
262	        INVENTORY_ITEM_MANAGE: "Create and edit items and their UoM conversions",
263	        INVENTORY_CATEGORY_READ: "Read item categories",
264	        INVENTORY_CATEGORY_MANAGE: "Create and edit item categories",
265	        INVENTORY_UOM_READ: "Read units of measure",
266	        INVENTORY_UOM_MANAGE: "Create and edit units of measure",
267	        INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_READ: "Read warehouses",
268	        INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_MANAGE: "Create and edit warehouses",
269	        INVENTORY_BIN_READ: "Read storage bins",
270	        INVENTORY_BIN_MANAGE: "Create and edit storage bins",
271	        INVENTORY_MOVE_READ: "Read the stock-move ledger and on-hand projections",
272	        INVENTORY_MOVE_CREATE: "Create stock moves (receipts, issues, transfers, adjustments)",
273	        INVENTORY_VALUATION_READ: "Read stock valuations and FIFO cost layers",
274	        INVENTORY_COUNT_READ: "Read stock counts and their variances",
275	        INVENTORY_COUNT_MANAGE: "Create stock counts and record counted quantities",
276	        INVENTORY_COUNT_POST: "Post stock-count variances as adjustment moves",
277	    },
278	)

1	"""App wiring: mount every module router + register the cross-module event handlers.
2	
3	A sanctioned core flat file (STRUCTURE §2 — cross-cutting app wiring): ``create_app`` in
4	``app.main`` stays focused on the app factory + middleware + exception handlers + health, and
5	delegates the two blocks that grow with every new module — the router mounting and the D-011
6	event-handler registration — to this file. Both are pure wiring with no business logic.
7	
8	``mount_routers(app)`` includes the core platform routers and every business-module router in the
9	fixed import order; ``register_event_handlers()`` subscribes the cross-module domain-event handlers
10	in the same deterministic module order (D-011).
11	"""
12	
13	from fastapi import FastAPI
14	
15	from app.core.docflow_router import router as docflow_router
16	from app.core.jobs_router import router as jobs_router
17	from app.core.security_router import router as security_router
18	from app.modules.crm.router import router as crm_router
19	from app.modules.finance.router import router as finance_router
20	from app.modules.hr.router import router as hr_router
21	from app.modules.inventory.router import router as inventory_router
22	from app.modules.maintenance.router import router as maintenance_router
23	from app.modules.manufacturing.router import router as manufacturing_router
24	from app.modules.procurement.router import router as procurement_router
25	from app.modules.projects.router import router as projects_router
26	from app.modules.quality.router import router as quality_router
27	from app.modules.reporting.router import router as reporting_router
28	from app.modules.sales.router import router as sales_router
29	
30	
31	def mount_routers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
32	    """Include the core platform routers + every business-module router, in the fixed import order.
33	
34	    The order here is also the D-011 handler-registration order (finance, then inventory, ...) once
35	    modules publish/subscribe events — kept aligned with ``register_event_handlers`` below."""
36	    # Core platform auth endpoints (D-008): login/refresh/logout/me at /api/v1/auth.
37	    app.include_router(security_router)
38	    # Core platform document-flow read endpoint (D-012): GET /api/v1/documents/{id}/chain.
39	    app.include_router(docflow_router)
40	    # Core platform background-job polling (PLAN 4P.5/D-032): GET /api/v1/jobs[/{id}].
41	    app.include_router(jobs_router)
42	    # Finance module (PLAN 4): chart of accounts + fiscal years/periods at /api/v1/finance.
43	    # First business module mounted; the fixed import order here is also the D-011 handler
44	    # registration order (finance, then inventory, ...) once modules publish/subscribe events.
45	    app.include_router(finance_router)
46	    # Inventory module (PLAN 5): item masters at /api/v1/inventory. Mounted after finance, the
47	    # D-011 handler-registration order; inventory reads finance/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5).
48	    app.include_router(inventory_router)
49	    # Procurement module (PLAN 6): vendor master at /api/v1/procurement. Mounted after inventory,
50	    # the D-011 handler-registration order; procurement OWNS the vendor entity and reads
51	    # finance/queries + inventory/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5 / D-029).
52	    app.include_router(procurement_router)
53	    # Sales module (PLAN 7): customer master + condition-style pricing at /api/v1/sales. Mounted
54	    # after procurement, the D-011 handler-registration order; sales OWNS the customer entity and
55	    # reads finance/queries + inventory/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5 / D-029). 7.1 publishes no
56	    # cross-module events (masters + pricing drive no effects; orders in 7.2 will).
57	    app.include_router(sales_router)
58	    # Manufacturing module (PLAN 8): PP master data (work centres, multi-level versioned BOMs,
59	    # routings) at /api/v1/manufacturing. Mounted after sales, the D-011 handler-registration
60	    # order; manufacturing reads finance/queries + inventory/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5 /

1	"""Domain events inventory PUBLISHES (D-011/D-020). Declarative data only — no logic, no models —
2	so finance's ``handlers.py`` may import these typed classes (the STRUCTURE §5 events.py allowance,
3	explicitly covering finance importing "upward" from inventory because events carry no behaviour).
4	
5	``StockValued`` is fired inside ``create_move`` AFTER the move + quant + valuation/layer updates,
6	carrying the computed value delta and the THREE GL account ids resolved from the item's category at
7	publish time (D-029 opaque ids). ``finance/handlers.py`` subscribes and posts the COGS/inventory
8	journal in the SAME transaction (D-011/D-020), so the move and its journal commit or roll back as
9	one
10	— a stock move can never exist without its journal entry, or vice versa.
11	
12	ONE event for every value-changing move; the handler branches on ``move_type`` for the per-type
13	postings (RECEIPT / ISSUE / ADJUSTMENT up/down). A value-neutral within-warehouse TRANSFER does NOT
14	publish (no value change → no journal). All amounts are full-precision Decimals; the handler
15	quantizes
16	the posted COGS to the currency's decimals (D-015).
17	"""
18	
19	import uuid
20	from decimal import Decimal
21	from typing import ClassVar
22	
23	from app.core.events import DomainEvent
24	from app.modules.inventory.constants import STOCK_VALUED_EVENT_KEY
25	
26	
27	class StockValued(DomainEvent):
28	    """A stock move changed valuation (D-020). Payload:
29	
30	    - ``move_id`` + ``move_date`` + ``move_number`` — the driving move (the journal posts with
31	      ``move_date``; a date in a CLOSED period makes the journal's period trigger fire inside the
32	      same transaction, rolling the whole move back — you cannot move stock into a closed period).
33	    - ``move_type`` — RECEIPT / ISSUE / ADJUSTMENT (the handler branches on it; TRANSFER within one
34	      warehouse never publishes). ``is_inbound`` disambiguates an ADJUSTMENT's direction (increase
35	      vs decrease) since both carry move_type ADJUSTMENT.
36	    - ``item_id`` + ``warehouse_id`` + ``quantity`` — the dimensions copied onto the COGS journal
37	      line (item dimension) and the value context.
38	    - ``total_cost`` — the value Δ the move moved (positive): RECEIPT entry value, ISSUE/decrease
39	      computed COGS, increase value. ``residual_to_price_difference`` is the moving-average
40	      zero-quantity flush amount (signed, usually 0) the handler posts to price-difference WITHIN
41	      the issue's entry so value and quantity never disagree (D-020).
42	    - ``document_id`` — the move's core_documents id (the docflow source ref the handler links the
43	      journal entry to, link_type 'posts').
44	    - ``inventory_account_id`` + ``offset_account_id`` — the two legs of the main posting: inventory
45	      is always one side; the OFFSET is chosen by the costing engine per move type (ISSUE -> COGS;
46	      RECEIPT / ADJUSTMENT -> price-difference; a reversal -> the OPPOSITE of the original move's
47	      offset, so reversing an issue credits COGS and reversing a receipt debits price-difference).
48	      ``is_inbound`` picks the Dr/Cr direction: inbound = Dr inventory / Cr offset.
49	    - ``price_difference_account_id`` — where the moving-average zero-quantity residual flush lands
50	      (always price-difference), separate from the main offset."""
51	
52	    key: ClassVar[str] = STOCK_VALUED_EVENT_KEY
53	
54	    move_id: uuid.UUID
55	    move_number: str
56	    move_type: str
57	    is_inbound: bool
58	    item_id: uuid.UUID
59	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID
60	    quantity: Decimal
61	    total_cost: Decimal
62	    residual_to_price_difference: Decimal
63	    move_date: str
64	    document_id: uuid.UUID
65	    inventory_account_id: uuid.UUID
66	    offset_account_id: uuid.UUID
67	    price_difference_account_id: uuid.UUID
68	
69	
70	__all__ = ["StockValued"]

2	bridges.
3	
4	TWO symmetric handlers. ``receive_goods_receipt_moves`` (INBOUND, below) creates RECEIPT moves for
5	a posted goods receipt; ``issue_delivery_moves`` (OUTBOUND, its twin, D-045) creates ISSUE moves for
6	a posted sales delivery. The KEY asymmetry: a receipt passes ``valuation_offset_account_id`` = the
7	GR/IR clearing account (so the move credits GR/IR); a delivery passes NO override, because an ISSUE
8	move's DEFAULT valuation offset IS the item-category COGS account (the costing engine routes an
9	ISSUE to COGS) — so a delivery posts Dr COGS / Cr Inventory with no account on the event. COGS *is*
10	the issue offset.
11	
12	Subscribes to ``procurement.goods_receipt.posted`` and creates one stock RECEIPT move per GR line in
13	the SAME transaction as the GR post (D-011 run_in_uow drains before commit). This is the SANCTIONED
14	cross-module mechanism (STRUCTURE §5): procurement must NOT import inventory's service, so the GR
15	post publishes ``GoodsReceiptPosted`` (a plain typed event — the only procurement file this handler
16	imports) and inventory reacts by calling its OWN ``stock_moves.create_move``. The mirror of the
17	existing inventory→finance pattern (inventory publishes StockValued, finance/handlers posts the
18	journal) — here procurement publishes, inventory handles.
19	
20	Each move passes ``valuation_offset_account_id`` = the GR/IR clearing account from the event, so the
21	move's costing event (StockValued) carries it as ``offset_account_id`` and finance's COGS handler
22	credits GR/IR — yielding Dr Inventory / Cr GR-IR (the three-way-match's clearing leg) instead of
23	the standalone price-difference offset. The whole chain — GR + N moves + N inventory-debit/GR-IR
24	journals — lands in ONE transaction; any failure (a closed receipt period trips a move's period
25	trigger, insufficient anything) rolls the WHOLE GR post back (D-020 all-or-nothing).
26	
27	The GR↔move linkage is recorded in DOCFLOW (GR document → 'moved_by' → move document, D-041), NOT a
28	cross-module FK — inventory owns the move, so it writes the edge from its side; procurement reads
29	the chain to render the flow. Procurement updates its own PO received_quantity + GR status in the

1	"""RBAC engine (D-009): code-defined permission catalog, permission resolution with a
2	short TTL cache, the require_permission dependency factory, and field-level read masking.
3	
4	The catalog is the source of truth: modules declare their permission keys in their
5	``constants.py`` and register them here at import time via ``register_permissions``;
6	``sync_permission_catalog`` upserts the registry into ``core_permissions`` so tenants
7	can only ever be granted keys that some code path actually checks. Roles and grants are
8	tenant data (core/models.py); resolution joins user_roles -> role_permissions ->
9	permissions in one query, memoized 60s keyed on (tenant_id, user_id, token_version).
10	"""
11	
12	import functools
13	import time
14	import uuid
15	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
16	from contextvars import ContextVar
17	from typing import Annotated, Any
18	
19	from fastapi import Depends
20	from pydantic import WrapSerializer
21	from pydantic_core.core_schema import SerializerFunctionWrapHandler
22	from sqlalchemy import select
23	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
24	
25	from app.core.exceptions import PermissionDeniedError
26	from app.core.models import Permission, RolePermission, UserRole
27	
28	# --- Permission catalog (code-defined source of truth) ------------------------
29	
30	# Module-level registry. Modules call register_permissions at import; the values are
31	# the human-readable descriptions seeded alongside the key. Insertion-ordered so the
32	# catalog sync and tests see a stable order.
33	_CATALOG: dict[str, str | None] = {}
34	
35	
36	def register_permissions(*keys: str, descriptions: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None:
37	    """Declare permission keys that exist in code (D-009). Idempotent: re-registering a
38	    key keeps the first description unless a new one is supplied. Modules call this at
39	    import from their ``constants.py`` (e.g. ``register_permissions(FIN_JOURNAL_POST)``)."""
40	    descriptions = descriptions or {}
41	    for key in keys:
42	        new_description = descriptions.get(key)
43	        if key not in _CATALOG or new_description is not None:
44	            _CATALOG[key] = new_description if new_description is not None else _CATALOG.get(key)
45	
46	
47	def catalog_keys() -> frozenset[str]:
48	    """The full set of code-declared permission keys (the grantable universe)."""
49	    return frozenset(_CATALOG)
50	
51	
52	# Core permission keys, registered at import (module __init__ files register theirs).
53	# Format is ``module.entity.action`` per STRUCTURE §7.
54	ADMIN_USER_MANAGE = "admin.user.manage"
55	ADMIN_ROLE_MANAGE = "admin.role.manage"
56	ADMIN_AUDIT_READ = "admin.audit.read"
57	ADMIN_TENANT_MANAGE = "admin.tenant.manage"
58	CORE_DOCUMENT_READ = "core.document.read"
59	CORE_SETTING_MANAGE = "core.setting.manage"
60	
61	register_permissions(
62	    ADMIN_USER_MANAGE,
63	    ADMIN_ROLE_MANAGE,
64	    ADMIN_AUDIT_READ,
65	    ADMIN_TENANT_MANAGE,
66	    CORE_DOCUMENT_READ,
67	    CORE_SETTING_MANAGE,
68	    descriptions={
69	        ADMIN_USER_MANAGE: "Create, edit and deactivate users",
70	        ADMIN_ROLE_MANAGE: "Create roles and assign permissions",
71	        ADMIN_AUDIT_READ: "Read the audit log",
72	        ADMIN_TENANT_MANAGE: "Manage tenant settings and provisioning",
73	        CORE_DOCUMENT_READ: "View documents and their flow",
74	        CORE_SETTING_MANAGE: "Manage tenant-level configuration",
75	    },
76	)
77	
78	
79	async def sync_permission_catalog(session: AsyncSession) -> int:
80	    """Upsert every code-declared key into core_permissions (D-009). Idempotent: existing
81	    keys are left as-is, only missing ones are inserted, so re-running creates no dupes.
82	    Permissions are GLOBAL data — callers run this under system_context (seed/provisioning).
83	    Returns the number of rows inserted this call."""
84	    existing = set(
85	        (await session.execute(select(Permission.key))).scalars().all()
86	    )
87	    inserted = 0
88	    for key, description in _CATALOG.items():
89	        if key in existing:
90	            continue
91	        session.add(Permission(key=key, description=description))
92	        inserted += 1
93	    await session.flush()
94	    return inserted
95	
96	
97	# --- Permission resolution + TTL cache (D-009) --------------------------------
98	
99	_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 60.0
100	# key -> (expires_at_monotonic, permissions). Process-local; multi-worker deploys lag
101	# per worker by at most the TTL, or instantly on token_version bump (the key changes).
102	_CACHE: dict[tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID, int], tuple[float, frozenset[str]]] = {}
103	
104	
105	def clear_cache() -> None:
106	    """Drop every cached resolution. Used by tests and a future global flush."""
107	    _CACHE.clear()
108	
109	
110	def invalidate(tenant_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID, token_version: int) -> None:
111	    """Evict one principal's cached permissions after a role change (D-009). Callers that
112	    only know (tenant, user) can pass any token_version they hold; on mismatch the stale
113	    entry simply expires within the TTL — but admin role mutations should pass the live
114	    token_version so the next request recomputes immediately."""
115	    _CACHE.pop((tenant_id, user_id, token_version), None)
116	
117	
118	async def _query_permissions(
119	    session: AsyncSession, user_id: uuid.UUID, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
120	) -> frozenset[str]:
121	    """ONE join: user_roles -> role_permissions -> permissions -> effective key set.
122	    Runs under the request's tenant context, so the user_roles/role_permissions rows are
123	    already tenant-filtered; the explicit user_id predicate narrows to this principal."""
124	    stmt = (
125	        select(Permission.key)
126	        .select_from(UserRole)
127	        .join(RolePermission, RolePermission.role_id == UserRole.role_id)
128	        .join(Permission, Permission.id == RolePermission.permission_id)
129	        .where(UserRole.user_id == user_id)
130	        .distinct()
131	    )
132	    keys = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all()
133	    return frozenset(keys)
134	
135	
136	async def resolve_permissions(
137	    session: AsyncSession,
138	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
139	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
140	    token_version: int,
141	    now: float | None = None,
142	) -> frozenset[str]:
143	    """Effective permission set for a principal, memoized 60s (D-009). ``now`` is an
144	    optional monotonic timestamp for deterministic tests; production uses time.monotonic.
145	    Tests prefer clear_cache()/invalidate() over advancing the clock."""
146	    clock = now if now is not None else time.monotonic()
147	    cache_key = (tenant_id, user_id, token_version)
148	    cached = _CACHE.get(cache_key)
149	    if cached is not None and cached[0] > clock:
150	        return cached[1]
151	    permissions = await _query_permissions(session, user_id, tenant_id)
152	    _CACHE[cache_key] = (clock + _CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, permissions)
153	    return permissions
154	
155	
156	# --- require_permission dependency factory (D-009) ----------------------------
157	
158	
159	def require_permission(key: str) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]:
160	    """FastAPI dependency factory: returns a dependency that loads the current principal
161	    (reusing get_current_user) and raises PermissionDeniedError (403, code
162	    ``rbac.permission_denied``, details naming the missing key) unless ``key`` is in the
163	    principal's resolved permissions. Attach per route via
164	    ``dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(ADMIN_USER_MANAGE))]``."""
165	
166	    # Imported here, not at module top, to avoid a core import cycle: deps imports rbac
167	    # (get_current_user resolves permissions) and rbac imports deps (this guard).
168	    from app.core.deps import CurrentUser, get_current_user
169	
170	    async def _dependency(
171	        current: Annotated[CurrentUser, Depends(get_current_user)],
172	    ) -> CurrentUser:
173	        if key not in current.permissions:
174	            raise PermissionDeniedError(
175	                code="rbac.permission_denied",
176	                message=f"Missing permission: {key}",
177	                details={"permission": key},
178	            )
179	        return current
180	
181	    return _dependency
182	
183	
184	# --- Field-level read masking (D-009) -----------------------------------------
185	
186	# Serialization-time principal permissions. Set by get_current_user per request and by
187	# the test ``permissions_context`` fixture; default empty so anything serialized OUTSIDE
188	# a request (jobs, tests without the fixture) fails CLOSED — masked fields read as None.
189	current_permissions: ContextVar[frozenset[str]] = ContextVar(
190	    "current_permissions", default=frozenset()
191	)
192	
193	def _mask_serializer(
194	    permission: str, value: Any, handler: SerializerFunctionWrapHandler
195	) -> Any:
196	    """WrapSerializer body (D-009): emit the real serialized value only when the guarding
197	    permission is present in current_permissions, else None. The permission is bound via
198	    functools.partial below — a WrapSerializer cannot read loose Annotated metadata."""
199	    if permission in current_permissions.get():
200	        return handler(value)
201	    return None
202	
203	
204	def Masked[T](tp: type[T], permission: str) -> Any:  # noqa: N802 - type-factory, PascalCase by design
205	    """Annotate a Pydantic field as read-masked behind ``permission`` (D-009).
206	
207	    Usage::
208	
209	        class EmployeeRead(ApiModel):
210	            base_salary: Masked(Decimal | None, "hr.compensation.read")
211	
212	    Serializes to the real value when current_permissions contains the key, else None.
213	    CONVENTION: masked fields are EXCLUDED from the entity's Create/Update schemas and
214	    edited through a separate permission-guarded endpoint, so a partial update can never
215	    silently null a masked field (the HR module enforces this for compensation)."""
216	    return Annotated[
217	        tp | None,
218	        WrapSerializer(functools.partial(_mask_serializer, permission)),
219	    ]

300	## D-016 — Custom fields: core-owned JSONB + metadata registry (ownership fixed)
301	
302	**Decision.**
303	**Ownership fix:** the draft put the registry and validator in `modules/industry`, which forces finance/inventory/hr services to import industry — an upward dependency violating STRUCTURE §5 (finance is the bottom of the import order); the parity doc itself assigns "metadata-driven field extensibility" to core. Therefore:
304	
305	**Registry table `core_custom_field_defs`** (id, tenant_id, entity_key like `'inventory.item'`, field_key validated by `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$`, label, field_type enum TEXT|NUMBER|DECIMAL|BOOLEAN|DATE|SELECT, is_required, options JSON for SELECT, validation JSON `{min,max,regex,max_length}`, display_group, display_order, is_active; UNIQUE(tenant_id, entity_key, field_key)) and its logic live in `core/custom_fields.py` — a new flat core file recorded in DECISIONS.md as a STRUCTURE §2 amendment.

307	It exposes:
308	
309	- `custom_fields_column()` returning `MutableDict.as_mutable(sa.JSON(none_as_null=False).with_variant(postgresql.JSONB(), 'postgresql'))`, NOT NULL server_default `'{}'`, applied by every extensible entity (item, vendor, customer, journal-entry header, sales/purchase docs, employee, equipment);
310	- `validate_custom_fields(session, tenant_id, entity_key, payload) -> dict`, called by owning-module services on create/update: loads active defs (per-request cached), rejects unknown keys, enforces required-on-create, coerces per type — DATE as ISO-8601 string, DECIMAL as string parsed via `Decimal` (never JSON float, consistent with D-015), NUMBER int, BOOLEAN bool, SELECT membership.
311	
312	Defs are WRITTEN by industry-template application at provisioning and by an admin CRUD endpoint (`/api/v1/admin/custom-field-defs`) — both call core service functions, keeping data ownership at the platform level while templates supply content. Pydantic schemas type the field `custom_fields: dict[str, Any] = {}`; the service validator is the gate.
313	
314	**Report builder** reads defs via core and builds portable expressions with `Model.custom_fields['key'].as_string()/.as_integer()/.as_boolean()` (renders `->>` on PG, `JSON_EXTRACT` on SQLite); DECIMAL sort/aggregation casts through Numeric on PG; on SQLite uses CAST to REAL and is documented display-grade. Keys are flat top-level scalars only (registry enforces no nesting). Optional Postgres-only GIN indexes ship in dialect-branched Alembic migrations when a template declares searchable fields; the SQLite arm is a no-op.
315	
316	**Rationale.**
317	One nullable-free JSON column per entity keeps migrations trivial when templates add fields; routing validation through the owning service preserves service-layer-owns-logic; and moving the registry to core resolves the dependency inversion cleanly — modules import core freely, so every module can validate without touching industry. The portable JSON path API confines all PG/SQLite JSON divergence to two call sites.
318	
319	**Rejected alternatives.**
320	- Industry-module ownership (the draft): upward imports from finance/inventory — a hard STRUCTURE violation; rejected outright rather than "interpreted around".
321	- EAV table: row explosion, painful reports.
322	- Per-field ALTER TABLE: per-tenant DDL is operationally dangerous and unexpressible in linear Alembic history.
323	- Dynamic per-tenant Pydantic models: runtime model building for zero gain over a dict validator.
324	- DECIMAL values as JSON numbers: floats by another name.
325	
326	**Risks & mitigations.**
327	- Custom fields are invisible to DB constraints — accepted: they are descriptive/reporting fields by design; anything participating in financial invariants must be a real column (rule recorded in `docs/modules/industry.md`).
328	- Field deactivation orphans stored values — `is_active` soft-deactivation only, never hard delete.
329	- `JSON_EXTRACT` vs `->>` nested-value divergence — moot under the flat-scalar restriction.
330	
331	---
332	
333	## D-017 — Universal journal schema, posting protocol, and reversal
334	
335	**Decision.**
336	`modules/finance/models.py`.
337	
338	**Header `fin_journal_entries`:** id `sa.Uuid` app-generated, tenant_id, entry_number text NULLABLE with partial unique index (tenant_id, entry_number) WHERE entry_number IS NOT NULL — FIXED from the draft's NOT NULL: numbers are claimed at POSTING per the D-012 claim-timing rule so abandoned drafts cannot burn gapless numbers; document_type enum (MANUAL, AP_INVOICE, AR_INVOICE, PAYMENT, COGS, FX_REVAL, DEPRECIATION, REVERSAL, …), status DRAFT|POSTED|REVERSED, posting_date, fiscal_period_id FK, currency_code (one transaction currency per entry; cross-currency events become multiple entries), functional_currency_code, exchange_rate RateType, description, posted_at, posted_by_user_id, reversal_of_entry_id self-FK UNIQUE, reversed_by_entry_id self-FK, DocumentMixin document_id. REMOVED from the draft: the header idempotency_key column — idempotency has exactly one home, `core_idempotency_keys` (two uncoordinated mechanisms invite divergence).
339	
340	**Lines `fin_journal_lines`:** id, tenant_id, entry_id FK, line_number (UNIQUE(entry_id, line_number)), account_id NOT NULL, nullable dimension FKs on every line (cost_center_id, profit_center_id, wbs_element_id, item_id, vendor_id, customer_id as typed FKs, warehouse_id, tax_code_id), quantity QuantityType + uom_code, MoneyType amount pairs debit_amount/credit_amount (transaction) and functional_debit_amount/functional_credit_amount, all NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; denormalized posting_date, fiscal_period_id, is_posted for projections.
341	
342	**DDL:** named CHECK `ck_fin_journal_lines_one_side`: `(debit_amount > 0 AND credit_amount = 0) OR (credit_amount > 0 AND debit_amount = 0)`; companion CHECK that functional amounts are non-negative, not both positive, and on the same side as the transaction side (functional zero allowed).
343	
344	**Functional balance fix:** the draft's separate rounding-difference line is impossible — a functional-only line has zero transaction amounts and violates the mandated one-side CHECK — so the residual functional cent from translation is absorbed into the largest line's functional amount via `core/money.py` `allocate()` (largest-remainder), making functional sums balance with no special lines.
345	
346	**Balance backstop:** per-dialect trigger on `fin_journal_entries` firing on the DRAFT→POSTED UPDATE, SUM-checking debits == credits over the entry's lines in BOTH currency pairs, raising `ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY` (plpgsql RAISE / SQLite `RAISE(ABORT)`) — exact on both engines per D-015.
347	
348	**Immutability:** BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE on lines raise `ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE` when the parent is POSTED; BEFORE INSERT on lines raises when the parent is already POSTED; BEFORE DELETE on POSTED headers raises; BEFORE UPDATE on POSTED headers raises UNLESS the only change is reversed_by_entry_id NULL→value plus status POSTED→REVERSED (explicit column-by-column OLD/NEW comparison in the WHEN clause, dedicated tests).
349	
350	**Posting protocol** (two explicit flushes — FIXED: the unit of work does not guarantee cross-table UPDATE order, so a single flush could update the header to POSTED before the line updates and trip the line-immutability triggers): the service loads the entry WITH all lines (needed anyway to validate sums in both currencies), validates balance and period, calls `docflow.assign_number()`, mutates the LOADED line objects (is_posted=True, posting_date, fiscal_period_id) — loaded-object mutation, never bulk `update()`, which both respects the audit bulk-write assertion and keeps diffs audited — then `session.flush()`; then sets header status=POSTED/posted_at/posted_by and flushes again (balance + period triggers fire here); then publishes `finance.journal.posted`; audit rows ride the same transaction automatically.
351	
352	**Reversal:** `post_reversal(entry_id, reversal_date, reason)` creates a NEW entry (document_type=REVERSAL, fresh number claimed at its posting, reversal_of_entry_id set) with every line copied dimension-identical and debit/credit swapped in BOTH currencies using the original frozen functional amounts (no re-translation), posted into an open period; then sets original.reversed_by_entry_id + status=REVERSED (the single sanctioned header mutation); both linked in docflow with link_type `'reverses'`. No deletes, no in-place edits, ever.
353	
354	**Rationale.**

1	"""The tax engine (PLAN 4.4): configurable tax codes + the calculation AP/AR/Sales call.
2	
3	Two concerns live here, both owned by the service layer (CLAUDE.md rule 7):
4	
5	1. **Calculation** (pure, no DB): ``calculate_line_tax`` turns one line's base amount + a tax code +
6	   a direction into a ``TaxCalculation`` (net / tax / gross + the account to post to), and
7	   ``calculate_document_tax`` groups many lines by tax code into the tax journal lines a document
8	   posts. The math is exact-decimal (D-015): every amount quantizes ROUND_HALF_UP to the currency's
9	   minor unit, and document-level grouping uses ``allocate`` so per-code tax sums reconstitute
10	   exactly with no stray rounding cent.
11	
12	2. **CRUD** (DB): create / update / list / get tax codes, validating that any wired posting account
13	   exists in the tenant. The DB UNIQUE(tenant_id, code) backstops the duplicate-code check.
14	
15	Inclusive vs exclusive (the SAP-style distinction):
16	- EXCLUSIVE: the line's base amount IS the net; tax is added on top. ``tax = net * rate``,
17	  ``gross = net + tax``.
18	- INCLUSIVE: the line's base amount IS the gross (tax already inside the price). ``net = gross /
19	  (1 + rate)``, ``tax = gross - net``. Deriving tax as ``gross - net`` (rather than ``gross * rate /
20	  (1+rate)`` directly) keeps net + tax == gross EXACTLY after quantization — the two rounded parts
21	  always reconstitute the rounded gross.
22	"""

28	from decimal import Decimal

2	
3	This is the ONE place that sets `current_tenant_id` for the request lifecycle from a
4	validated access token; the pure-ASGI middleware in app.main resets it in a finally
5	block so request A's tenant never leaks to request B on the same worker.
6	"""

9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	from typing import Annotated
11

27	# surface rather than reaching into core.db / core.config directly.
28	__all__ = [
29	    "CurrentUser",
30	    "CurrentUserDep",
31	    "SessionDep",
32	    "SessionFactoryDep",
33	    "get_current_user",
34	    "get_session",
35	    "get_session_factory",
36	    "get_settings",
37	]
38	
39	# auto_error=False: a missing/blank header must surface as the D-014 auth envelope
40	# (AuthError -> 401), not Starlette's bare 403 HTTPException.
41	_bearer_scheme = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)
42	
43	# Annotated dependency aliases: the modern FastAPI idiom that keeps Depends() out of
44	# parameter defaults (ruff B008) and lets routers share one typed handle.
45	SessionDep = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)]
46	# The sessionmaker dependency (test-overridable like get_session). Job-submitting routers pass
47	# it to schedule_job post-commit so the runner opens its sessions against the SAME database —
48	# the app factory in production, the per-test engine's factory under the conftest override.
49	SessionFactoryDep = Annotated[async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession], Depends(get_session_factory)]
50	_CredentialsDep = Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(_bearer_scheme)]
51	
52	
53	@dataclass(frozen=True)
54	class CurrentUser:
55	    """Resolved request principal (D-008/D-009). `permissions` is the effective key set
56	    resolved by RBAC (one join query, cached 60s)."""
57	
58	    user_id: uuid.UUID
59	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
60	    permissions: frozenset[str]
61	    token_version: int
62	
63	
64	async def get_current_user(
65	    credentials: _CredentialsDep,
66	    session: SessionDep,
67	) -> CurrentUser:
68	    if credentials is None:
69	        raise AuthError(message="Missing bearer token", code="auth.invalid_token")
70	
71	    claims = decode_token(credentials.credentials, expected_typ="access")
72	    try:
73	        user_id = uuid.UUID(claims["sub"])
74	        tenant_id = uuid.UUID(claims["tenant_id"])
75	        claim_version = int(claims["ver"])
76	    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
77	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token") from exc
78	
79	    # Set the tenancy ContextVar FROM the validated token (D-007 production setter):
80	    # the user lookup below then runs under the token's tenant, so a tampered
81	    # tenant_id can only ever resolve a user that actually belongs to that tenant —
82	    # cross-tenant access is impossible. The middleware resets this in a finally block.
83	    current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
84	
85	    user = (
86	        await session.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
87	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
88	    if user is None or not user.is_active:
89	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
90	    if user.token_version != claim_version:
91	        # Stale token after a "revoke everything" bump (D-008).
92	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
93	
94	    # RBAC resolution (D-009): one join query, memoized 60s on
95	    # (tenant_id, user_id, token_version). Runs under the tenant context set above, so
96	    # the user_roles/role_permissions rows are already tenant-filtered.
97	    permissions = await resolve_permissions(
98	        session, user.id, user.tenant_id, user.token_version
99	    )
100	    # Serialization-time masking (D-009) reads this ContextVar; the middleware resets it
101	    # in a finally block alongside current_tenant_id so it never leaks across requests.
102	    current_permissions.set(permissions)
103	    # D-010 audit context: now that the principal is known, stamp the actor onto every
104	    # audit row this request writes. The middleware seeded it None (system) and resets it.
105	    actor_user_id_ctx.set(user.id)
106	
107	    return CurrentUser(
108	        user_id=user.id,
109	        tenant_id=user.tenant_id,
110	        permissions=permissions,
111	        token_version=user.token_version,
112	    )
113	
114	
115	CurrentUserDep = Annotated[CurrentUser, Depends(get_current_user)]

86	@dataclass
87	class QueryCounter:
88	    """Counts real SQL statements executed on the per-test engine while active.
89	
90	    Used as a context manager: ``with query_counter() as qc: ...`` then read ``qc.count``.
91	    The ``after_cursor_execute`` listener attaches to the TEST engine's sync engine on enter
92	    and detaches on exit (per-use, so the per-test engine pattern stays leak-free).
93	    Transaction-control statements (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT/RELEASE) and PRAGMAs are
94	    excluded — the budget measures real SELECT/INSERT/... statements. ``statements`` keeps
95	    the counted SQL so a budget failure shows exactly which queries ran.
96	    """

98	    sync_engine: Engine
99	    count: int = 0
100	    statements: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
101	
102	    _IGNORED_PREFIXES = ("BEGIN", "COMMIT", "ROLLBACK", "SAVEPOINT", "RELEASE", "PRAGMA")

104	    def _after_cursor_execute(
105	        self,
106	        conn: Any,
107	        cursor: Any,
108	        statement: str,
109	        parameters: Any,
110	        context: Any,
111	        executemany: bool,
112	    ) -> None:
113	        if statement.lstrip().upper().startswith(self._IGNORED_PREFIXES):
114	            return
115	        self.count += 1
116	        self.statements.append(statement)
117	
118	    def __enter__(self) -> "QueryCounter":
119	        self.count = 0
120	        self.statements = []
121	        event.listen(self.sync_engine, "after_cursor_execute", self._after_cursor_execute)
122	        return self

124	    def __exit__(
125	        self,
126	        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
127	        exc: BaseException | None,
128	        tb: TracebackType | None,
129	    ) -> None:
130	        event.remove(self.sync_engine, "after_cursor_execute", self._after_cursor_execute)

"""Typed custom fields (D-016): the core-owned registry + validator + JSON column helper.

A STRUCTURE §2 amendment: this flat core file is the platform-level home for tenant-defined
custom fields, so EVERY module (finance is the bottom of the import order) can validate a custom
payload without importing the industry module — the industry layer (PLAN 14.1) is the first
WRITER of defs, but the registry and validator are core so the dependency direction stays
modules -> core (D-016 ownership fix; the draft put this in modules/industry, an upward import).

Three pieces, exactly as D-016 prescribes:

* ``CustomFieldDef`` (``core_custom_field_defs``) — one registered field for an entity, e.g. a
  ``barcode`` STRING on ``inventory.item``. ``entity_key`` is the dotted module.entity string the
  owning module passes; ``field_key`` is a flat scalar key (``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$``).
  UNIQUE(tenant_id, entity_key, field_key). Soft-deactivation via ``is_active`` (never hard delete,
  so stored values are not orphaned).

* ``validate_custom_fields(defs, values) -> dict`` — validate a custom_fields payload against the
  registered defs for ONE entity: unknown keys rejected, required enforced, each value coerced per
  type. The portable-JSON rules (D-015/D-016): DATE as an ISO-8601 string, DECIMAL as a STRING
  parsed via ``Decimal`` (never a JSON float), NUMBER an int, BOOL a bool. Flat scalars only —
  a dict/list value is rejected. The result is a plain JSON-portable dict the owning service
  stores in its ``custom_fields`` column.

* ``custom_fields_column()`` — the ``JSON_VARIANT`` column (JSONB on PG, JSON elsewhere) an
  extensible entity opts into, NOT NULL defaulting to ``{}``. Custom fields are descriptive /
  reporting fields by design: they are invisible to DB constraints, so anything participating in a
  financial invariant must be a real column (rule recorded in docs/modules/industry.md).

The CRUD service functions (``create_field_def`` / ``list_field_defs`` / ``deactivate_field_def``)
are the sanctioned write path — the industry template loader and a future admin endpoint both call
them, keeping data ownership at the platform level while templates supply content.
"""

from datetime import date

from enum import StrEnum

# Flat scalar key: lowercase, starts with a letter, <=50 chars. The same shape STRUCTURE §7 uses
# for snake_case identifiers; enforced at def-create so report-builder JSON paths stay portable.
FIELD_KEY_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$")
# entity_key is the dotted module.entity the owning module passes, e.g. "inventory.item".
ENTITY_KEY_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$")


class CustomFieldType(StrEnum):
    """The value types a custom field may hold (D-016). Stored as the UPPER value on the def row;
    the validator coerces a payload value to the matching Python type (DECIMAL via string, never a
    JSON float — consistent with D-015's no-float rule)."""

    STRING = "STRING"
    NUMBER = "NUMBER"
    DECIMAL = "DECIMAL"
    BOOL = "BOOL"
    DATE = "DATE"


class CustomFieldDef(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """One registered custom field for an entity (D-016). The owning module reads the active defs
    for its ``entity_key`` and passes them to ``validate_custom_fields`` on create/update. Audited
    (D-010): the field registry is tenant configuration — adding/deactivating a field changes what
    a form and the report builder surface."""

    __tablename__ = "core_custom_field_defs"
    __table_args__ = (
        # Explicit uq name: the D-022 convention keys on column 0 (tenant_id) only and would
        # collide with any other UNIQUE on this table starting with tenant_id.
        sa.UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id",
            "entity_key",
            "field_key",
            name="uq_core_custom_field_defs_tenant_id_entity_key_field_key",
        ),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        # The owning-module read path: "active defs for this entity" filters (tenant, entity_key).
        sa.Index(
            "ix_core_custom_field_defs_tenant_id_entity_key", "tenant_id", "entity_key"
        ),
    )

    entity_key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(80), nullable=False)
    field_key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(50), nullable=False)
    label: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
    # Stored as the CustomFieldType UPPER value (the core/finance no-sa.Enum convention).
    data_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(10), nullable=False)
    is_required: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
    )
    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=True, server_default=sa.true()
    )
    # The default value, stored portably as a STRING (rendered the same as a payload value would be
    # — DECIMAL/DATE as strings) and applied by the validator when the key is absent.
    default_value: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)


def custom_fields_column() -> Mapped[dict[str, Any]]:
    """A NOT-NULL JSON_VARIANT column (JSONB on PG, JSON elsewhere) for an extensible entity's
    custom_fields, defaulting to ``{}`` (D-016). An entity opts in by declaring
    ``custom_fields: Mapped[dict[str, Any]] = custom_fields_column()`` — keys are flat top-level
    scalars only; the owning service is the validation gate via ``validate_custom_fields``."""
    return mapped_column(
        JSON_VARIANT,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
        server_default=sa.text("'{}'"),
    )


def _coerce_value(definition: CustomFieldDef, raw: Any) -> Any:
    """Coerce one payload value to the def's type, raising ValidationFailedError on mismatch.

    Flat scalars only — a dict/list is rejected outright (D-016: no nesting). DECIMAL is parsed
    from a STRING via ``Decimal`` and re-emitted as a string (never a JSON float, D-015); DATE is an
    ISO-8601 string validated and normalized; NUMBER is an int; BOOL a bool; STRING a str."""
    if isinstance(raw, (dict, list)):
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message=f"Custom field '{definition.field_key}' must be a flat scalar value",
            code="custom_fields.not_scalar",
            details={"field": definition.field_key},
        )
    data_type = CustomFieldType(definition.data_type)
    try:
        if data_type is CustomFieldType.STRING:
            return str(raw)
        if data_type is CustomFieldType.NUMBER:
            # A bool is an int subclass; reject it so a NUMBER field never silently stores True.
            if isinstance(raw, bool):
                raise ValueError
            return int(raw)
        if data_type is CustomFieldType.DECIMAL:
            # DECIMAL MUST arrive as a string (D-015 no-float): a float is rejected, an int/str is
            # parsed exactly and re-emitted as the canonical string form.
            if isinstance(raw, float):
                raise ValueError
            return str(Decimal(str(raw)))
        if data_type is CustomFieldType.BOOL:
            if not isinstance(raw, bool):
                raise ValueError
            return raw
        if data_type is CustomFieldType.DATE:
            # Validate + normalize to ISO-8601; reject a non-string or a non-date string.
            return date.fromisoformat(str(raw)).isoformat()
    except (ValueError, TypeError, InvalidOperation) as exc:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message=(
                f"Custom field '{definition.field_key}' is not a valid {data_type.value}"
            ),
            code="custom_fields.type_mismatch",
            details={"field": definition.field_key, "expected": data_type.value},
        ) from exc
    raise ValidationFailedError(  # pragma: no cover - exhaustive enum, defensive
        message=f"Unsupported custom field type {definition.data_type}",
        code="custom_fields.unsupported_type",
    )


def validate_custom_fields(
    defs: list[CustomFieldDef], values: dict[str, Any] | None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate a ``custom_fields`` payload against an entity's registered defs (D-016).

    - Unknown keys (no active def) are REJECTED — a custom payload may only carry registered fields.
    - Each present value is coerced to its def's type (DECIMAL as string, DATE ISO, etc.).
    - A required field absent from the payload uses the def's ``default_value`` when set, else raises.
    - An optional field absent from the payload is simply omitted from the result.

    Returns a fresh JSON-portable dict the owning service stores. Only ACTIVE defs are considered —
    callers load defs via ``list_field_defs(..., active_only=True)``."""
    values = values or {}
    by_key = {definition.field_key: definition for definition in defs}
    unknown = sorted(set(values) - set(by_key))
    if unknown:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="Unknown custom field(s)",
            code="custom_fields.unknown_keys",
            details={"keys": unknown},
        )
    result: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, definition in by_key.items():
        if key in values and values[key] is not None:
            result[key] = _coerce_value(definition, values[key])
        elif definition.default_value is not None:
            result[key] = _coerce_value(definition, definition.default_value)
        elif definition.is_required:
            raise ValidationFailedError(
                message=f"Custom field '{key}' is required",
                code="custom_fields.required",
                details={"field": key},
            )
    return result


# --- CRUD service (the sanctioned write path: industry loader + admin endpoint) ----------------


async def list_field_defs(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    entity_key: str,
    *,
    active_only: bool = True,
) -> list[CustomFieldDef]:
    """The active (or all) registered defs for an entity, ordered by field_key for stable forms
    and reports (D-016). Owning-module services call this with ``active_only=True`` to gate a
    payload."""
    stmt = select(CustomFieldDef).where(
        CustomFieldDef.tenant_id == tenant_id,
        CustomFieldDef.entity_key == entity_key,
    )
    if active_only:
        stmt = stmt.where(CustomFieldDef.is_active.is_(True))
    stmt = stmt.order_by(CustomFieldDef.field_key)
    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())


async def get_field_def(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, entity_key: str, field_key: str
) -> CustomFieldDef | None:
    """One def by its natural key (tenant, entity_key, field_key); None if not registered. Used by
    the idempotent loader's get-or-create."""
    stmt = select(CustomFieldDef).where(
        CustomFieldDef.tenant_id == tenant_id,
        CustomFieldDef.entity_key == entity_key,
        CustomFieldDef.field_key == field_key,
    )
    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()


async def create_field_def(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    entity_key: str,
    field_key: str,
    label: str,
    data_type: str,
    is_required: bool = False,
    default_value: str | None = None,
) -> CustomFieldDef:
    """Register a custom field (D-016). Validates the entity_key / field_key shapes and the type,
    then inserts; a duplicate (tenant, entity_key, field_key) raises ConflictError (the DB UNIQUE
    backstops). The idempotent loader calls ``ensure_field_def`` instead, which get-or-creates."""
    if not ENTITY_KEY_PATTERN.match(entity_key):
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="entity_key must be a dotted module.entity string",
            code="custom_fields.invalid_entity_key",
            details={"entity_key": entity_key},
        )
    if not FIELD_KEY_PATTERN.match(field_key):
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="field_key must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$",
            code="custom_fields.invalid_field_key",
            details={"field_key": field_key},
        )
    # Validate the type up front so a bad data_type fails at registration, not at first payload.
    coerced_type = CustomFieldType(data_type)
    if await get_field_def(session, tenant_id, entity_key, field_key) is not None:
        raise ConflictError(
            message=f"Custom field '{field_key}' already exists for {entity_key}",
            code="custom_fields.duplicate",
            details={"entity_key": entity_key, "field_key": field_key},
        )
    definition = CustomFieldDef(
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        entity_key=entity_key,
        field_key=field_key,
        label=label,
        data_type=coerced_type.value,
        is_required=is_required,
        default_value=default_value,
    )
    session.add(definition)
    await session.flush()
    return definition


async def ensure_field_def(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    entity_key: str,
    field_key: str,
    label: str,
    data_type: str,
    is_required: bool = False,
    default_value: str | None = None,
) -> CustomFieldDef:
    """Idempotent get-or-create for a custom field (D-016), used by the industry template loader so
    re-applying a template never duplicates a def. Returns the existing row UNCHANGED if the
    (tenant, entity_key, field_key) is already registered, otherwise creates it."""
    existing = await get_field_def(session, tenant_id, entity_key, field_key)
    if existing is not None:
        return existing
    return await create_field_def(
        session,
        tenant_id,
        entity_key=entity_key,
        field_key=field_key,
        label=label,
        data_type=data_type,
        is_required=is_required,
        default_value=default_value,
    )


async def deactivate_field_def(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, entity_key: str, field_key: str
) -> CustomFieldDef:
    """Soft-deactivate a field (D-016: never hard delete — stored values must not be orphaned).
    Mutates the loaded object so the audit diff is captured (D-010)."""
    definition = await get_field_def(session, tenant_id, entity_key, field_key)
    if definition is None:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message=f"Custom field '{field_key}' is not registered for {entity_key}",
            code="custom_fields.not_found",
            details={"entity_key": entity_key, "field_key": field_key},
        )
    definition.is_active = False
    await session.flush()
    return definition
